To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the length of female palate was significantly shorter than that of male palate, the location of greater palatal foramen was most commonly found palatal to the first molar, the branching point of GPA was mostly found at the level of the first and second premolar, the location of incisive fossae was most frequently found between the maxillary central incisors.
the greater palatines foramen was located most commonly at the palatal to the 2nd molar and the GPA was branching at the level of the first and 2nd molars together.
the location of greater palatin foramen and the branching point of the greater palatin artery are variable and should be carefully examined prior to harvesting of subepithelial graft from palate.
In summary, our research is concerned with
anatomical study of the palatal structures, which is the important factor for the periodontal surgeons in planning and harvesting the sub-epithelial connect tissue graft from the palate.
the anatomy of the greater palatal artery and its related structures in the palate.
the anatomy of palatine greater palatine vessels and their related structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the greater palatines foramen is most frequently located palatal to the first molar, the greater palatins artery is commonly found at the level of the second premolar or first molar, and the incisive fossae are located in the mid-palate area.
the palatal connective tissue graft is a safe and reliable source for soft tissue augmentation procedures in the oral cavity.
the greater palatinal structures are more variable in women and the palatal vault is wider and more variable in men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the palatal grafts should be harvested from the area between the maxillary first premolars and second molars.
the anatomical location of GPA is not a constant and that it varies from individual to individual.
the anatomical location of GPA and greater palatine foramens are different between genders.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to harvest the grafts of at least 5mm in height from the area of palate between maxillary first and second premolar in the majority of cases.
GPA is the main blood supply for the palatal soft tissues, and it is important to know its topography and the dimensions of the palatal area to avoid its injury.
the palatal vault is a good donor site for the graft harvesting, as long as it is done with caution.
